referents.why: 'him' is the addressee of 'go to Pharaoh and tell him'; Pharaoh is the only masculine singular person the command names.
referents.category: pronoun of an addressee named in the same command

referents.why: 'my people' sits inside the LORD's quoted message (turn1, frame cl3), so the speaker is the LORD.
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'me' in 'that they may serve me' is the speaker of the quoted message, the LORD.
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: the imperative 'go' is addressed to Moses, whom the LORD speaks to in cl0.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the speech's addressee

referents.why: 'you will say to him' is the second command of the same collection, addressed to Moses.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the speech's addressee

referents.why: 'let my people go' is the LORD's message delivered to Pharaoh (cl2 'say to him'); the implied 'you' is Pharaoh, masculine singular.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 'they may serve' takes plural agreement with the collective 'people' (w17), the only candidate; the noun is masculine singular in form, so the agreement is ad sensum.

links.why: a clause cannot be 'and then' itself; the builder link is a self-loop.
a weqatal after an imperative continues it ('go, and you will say'); the waw is fused into the verb, so 'then'.
a command followed by a yiqtol in a different person is a purpose, not a plain 'and'.
'let them go, that they may serve me': the release is for the worship.
the LORD says to Moses a run of commands joined by 'and'; the content is the whole imperative group.
'you will say to him' introduces the message, which begins with 'thus he says Yahweh'.
the quotative 'thus he says' introduces the single command 'let my people go'.

groups.why: the LORD speaks to Moses; the outer turn holds the commands and the commanded turn of Moses as parts. The builder listed the commands as direct parts.
groups.category: outer turn with commanded turn as part

groups.why: 'go' and 'say to him' are two commands joined by one waw, one collection; 'part' is not a role of an imperative group.
the commanded words are spoken by Moses to Pharaoh, and they quote the LORD, so they form a turn whose part is the innermost quoted turn.
the quoted message of the LORD to Pharaoh, whose part is the one command with its aim.
'let go' with 'that they may serve me' is a command with its aim; 'part' is not an imperative role.
